question.text: Let <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> be the two lines which are normal to <math><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> and tangent to <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>y</mi></math> respectively (where, <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are not the <math><mi>x</mi></math>-axis). Then, the product of the slopes of <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is

solution.text:
Let the slope of the tangent be k, then

the equation of the tangent to x2=-12y is kx=y+-3k2

Let the slope of the normal be m, then
the equation of the normal to y2=4x is y=mx-2m-m3
⇒k=m and 2m+m3=-3k2
⇒mm2+3m+2=0⇒m=-1,-2 (m=0 is rejected)
